feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 4 (20 mm spacing, span ±0.04 m, lead 0.07 m) scored 61.45, the best so far, with the oval at progress 0.167, the s-bend at 0.163 and the slalom up to 47.8. Iteration 2 (lead 0.07 m, 15 mm spacing) scored 60.41, and iteration 3 (lead 0.08 m) scored 60.33, so lead has saturated. Line_loss_events stayed at 1 per run in iteration 4, which fits the capture limit of about 0.0585 m for the ±0.04 m sensors. Depending on the next race: if line_loss_events falls below 1 and max_error stays below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, keep the ±0.06 m span. If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.17 with seven sensors, reduce the outer weights. If progress is still flat near 0.16 on the s-bend with line loss at 1, sensing is no longer the limit and wheel_radius should be the next lever.
requested_changes: If the slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.17 with the ±0.06 m row (iteration 4 slalom was 0.153), reduce the outer sensor span to ±0.05 m or state the spacing that works best, citing the iteration 4 oscillation data.

If line_loss_events stays at 1 and the s-bend progress is still about 0.16 after the span change (iterations 1 to 3 all gave 0.160 at different leads), try wheel_radius 0.035 m for more ground speed, because lead and span changes have not moved the s-bend.

If the oval and s-bend improve with the wider row but the robot still ends off track, try sensor_size 0.016 m at 20 mm spacing so the outer footprints stay on the 25 mm tape at the edge offsets, citing the iteration 4 telemetry where max_error reached 0.062 m.
